title: Reduced Chirp Gradient Defect-Cavity with Frozen Seed (21 Layers)
scientific_hypothesis: Gentler chirp slopes (60% reduced gradient) prevent over-optimization-induced passband degradation while maintaining stopband suppression; frozen seed from iteration 16 best candidate prevents catastrophic thickness drift.
design_principle: Defective DBR bandpass filter with (HL)^5 D (LH)^5 topology. Initial thicknesses from iteration 16 gradient_thickness__01 candidate. Chirp gradient scaled to 0.4× original magnitude. Per-layer perturbation capped at ±8 nm between optimization rounds.
proposed_topology: Air | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 (cavity) | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Ta2O5 | SiO2 | Fused Silica. Total 21 finite layers.
design_variables: layer thicknesses with ±8 nm round-to-round perturbation cap
chirp gradient scaling factor fixed at 0.4
manufacturing_considerations: ±8 nm perturbation cap reflects realistic thickness control between deposition runs
Ta2O5/SiO2 material pair has established deposition processes
theory_basis: Defective DBR structure (HL)^N D (LH)^N creates transmission resonance at defect wavelength
Chirped layer thicknesses broaden stopband rejection while maintaining narrow passband
Gradient optimization with bounded perturbations prevents local minima trapping
expected_advantages: Preserves iteration 16 high score (0.9831) while testing gentler optimization trajectory
Frozen seed prevents divergence from proven high-performing region
Reduced chirp may improve robustness to thickness errors
known_risks: Over-constrained perturbation cap may limit optimizer exploration
Gentler chirp may reduce stopband suppression bandwidth
Score may plateau below iteration 16 best if chirp reduction is excessive
execution_request_english: Design a 21-layer defect-cavity bandpass filter on fused silica substrate using Ta2O5 (high index) and SiO2 (low index). Layer sequence: Ta2O5/SiO2 alternating for 10 layers, central SiO2 cavity layer, then Ta2O5/SiO2 alternating for 10 layers. Initialize thicknesses from iteration 16 candidate gradient_thickness__01 vector. Apply chirp gradient scaling factor of 0.4 to initial thickness distribution. Constrain per-layer thickness perturbation to ±8 nm maximum change between consecutive optimization rounds. Optimize for maximum transmittance at 1550 nm with suppression in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Normal incidence, unpolarized illumination. Total layer count exactly 21. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 1400-1500 nm, 1550-1550 nm, 1600-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance at 1550 nm (soft target ≥ 0.95); strong suppression of transmittance in 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 1400-1500 nm; transmittance in 1600-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30.
revision_reason: Response to iteration 20 score regression (0.9831→0.8431). Apply feedback directive: reduce chirp gradient by 60%, apply ±8 nm perturbation cap, reinitialize from iteration 16 candidate pool as frozen seed to prevent thickness drift while testing gentler chirp slopes.
